annotations.summary: Advisory acceptance rate dropped below threshold over rolling 24h KPI window

evidence: Alert is self-monitoring (meta_self class): no namespace/pod/workload identity for a customer-cluster fault. omni_kpi_advisory_acceptance_rate computed from omni:kpi:z:{tenant}:accepted|rejected ZSET rolling 24h window.

Common cause in low-traffic/lab environments: sample size too small (few operator accept/reject actions in the 24h window) makes the ratio statistically noisy, not a real regression. Check sample count before treating as a quality regression.
root_cause: OmniAdvisoryAcceptanceRateLow is a KPI self-alert about Omni's own advisory quality, not a cluster fault — there is nothing to mutate. It fires when accepted/(accepted+rejected) over the rolling 24h window drops under the alert threshold, which in low-volume lab/staging environments is usually a small-sample artifact rather than a genuine model regression.

verification_steps.rationale: Check sample size (accepted+rejected) before trusting the ratio; <20 samples/24h is not statistically meaningful
Confirm whether the drop is a step change (real regression) or noise around a small denominator

proposed_remediation: step: No cluster mutation applicable (meta_self, mutate_eligible=False). If sample size is small, treat as informational and re-check after 24h of more traffic.
step: If sample size is adequate and rate is genuinely low, review recent advisory_golden benchmark scores (make benchmark-advisory) for a real quality regression in the LLM/RAG pipeline.
step: Escalate to on-call only if rate stays low across >=2 consecutive rolling windows with adequate sample size.

annotations.summary: Worker health server has not pushed a fresh check state recently; last_message_age exceeded threshold

evidence: Self-monitoring alert from health_server.py /healthz check 'last_message_age' (>600s = unhealthy). No customer namespace/pod target — the fault target IS the Omni worker pod itself.

Distinguish from a generic pod crash: this can mean the consumer loop is alive but Kafka has no new messages (idle, not stalled), or it can mean the asyncio loop is genuinely blocked (deadlock, hung LLM call).
root_cause: Omni worker's kafka_evidence_loop has not called record_message_processed() within the health-check window, indicating either a genuinely idle topic (no traffic) or a blocked consumer loop (deadlock, stuck synchronous call inside async context, Kafka rebalance hang).

verification_steps.rationale: Confirm degraded/unhealthy check and which check_name (kafka_lag/last_message_age) is failing
Look for rebalance loops or absence of any recent log lines (confirms hang vs idle)

verification_steps.command: kubectl exec -n multi-agent kafka-0 -- kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 --describe --group omni-evidence-consumer
verification_steps.rationale: Check consumer group lag — high/growing lag with no commits confirms a stuck consumer, not idle topic

proposed_remediation: step: No mutation on customer cluster (meta_self). If consumer group lag is high and growing with no progress, restart the omni-fullstack pod (kubectl rollout restart deploy/omni-fullstack -n multi-agent) — approval_required.
step: If topic genuinely has no new messages (idle, lag=0), this is a false positive from low traffic; no action needed.

annotations.summary: Worker health check redis_ping failing — cannot reach Redis

evidence: Self-monitoring alert: redis_ping check in health_server.py fails. This is an Omni-internal dependency failure, not a customer workload fault.
Common cause: redis-0 pod restarted and is still loading a large RDB snapshot (BusyLoadingError) — worker should self-heal once load completes, this is expected transient behavior, not a hard outage.
root_cause: Omni worker cannot establish/maintain a connection to its Redis backing store (state cache, RAG, dedup keys, audit chain head). Frequently transient: redis-0 pod restart triggers RDB reload (can take 60-130s for large datasets), during which BusyLoadingError is returned and ping fails by design until load completes.

verification_steps.rationale: Confirm redis-0 pod status (Running vs CrashLoopBackOff vs restarting)

verification_steps.command: kubectl logs -n multi-agent redis-0 --tail=50 | grep -i 'loading\|ready to accept'
verification_steps.rationale: Distinguish transient RDB-loading window from a genuine outage

verification_steps.command: kubectl exec -n multi-agent redis-0 -- redis-cli PING
verification_steps.rationale: Direct connectivity probe independent of the worker's own health check

proposed_remediation: step: No mutation needed if redis-0 is Running and actively loading RDB — wait for load to complete (worker's redis_loading_wait retry logic self-heals).
step: If redis-0 is CrashLoopBackOff or unreachable beyond the expected load window, investigate pod logs for OOM/disk and restart only with on-call approval — approval_required.

annotations.summary: Worker health check llm_up has reported 0 (down) for a sustained period

evidence: Self-monitoring alert: Ollama (qwen2.5-coder:7b) unreachable from the worker for a sustained window. Advisory/diagnosis pipeline degrades to deterministic-only short-circuits (contrast checks, SIEM lane) since LLM calls cannot complete.
AdvisoryModeKillSwitch and CRAT fail-closed paths are unaffected — this only blocks RAG/LLM reasoning paths, not deterministic ones.
root_cause: Ollama host (host.orb.internal:11434 in lab) is unreachable or the model is not loaded/responding, so analyst LLM calls time out or error, degrading the worker's llm_up health check to 0.

verification_steps.rationale: Confirm Ollama host is reachable and qwen2.5-coder:7b model is listed/loaded
Confirm whether failures are connection-refused (host down) vs timeout (model overloaded/slow)

proposed_remediation: step: No cluster mutation (meta_self, infra dependency outside K8s). If Ollama host process is down, restart it on the host — outside Omni's K8s RBAC scope, requires host-level access.

step: While LLM is down, expect advisory pipeline to rely on deterministic short-circuits only (contrast, SIEM lane); monitor for an uptick in RAG_MISS/SDK_ESCALATE terminal events as an indirect symptom.

annotations.summary: False-positive rate KPI (advisories later marked fail/executor_fail) exceeded threshold over rolling 24h window

evidence: Self-monitoring alert: omni_kpi_false_positive_rate computed from outcome=fail|executor_fail entries in omni:kpi:z:{tenant}:false_positive ZSET. No single cluster target — the signal aggregates across all advisories in the window.
High false-positive rate after a chaos-drill or load-test session is expected (synthetic faults intentionally probe edge cases) and should not be conflated with organic production false positives.
root_cause: A higher-than-normal share of recent advisories were marked as false positives (executor reported fail, or HITL rejected as incorrect diagnosis) within the rolling 24h KPI window — could indicate an RAG/LLM diagnosis quality regression, OR could be explained by recent chaos-drill/synthetic testing activity inflating the denominator.

verification_steps.rationale: Check sample size and whether the spike correlates with a specific time window
Cross-check against known chaos-drill/E2E test runs (timestamps) before treating as organic regression

proposed_remediation: step: No cluster mutation (meta_self). If spike correlates with chaos-drill/E2E test traffic, this is expected — no action.
step: If no synthetic testing in the window, run make benchmark-advisory and review tests/benchmarks/advisory_golden cases for a genuine LLM/RAG quality regression.
